no_tuning_statement: No decoding parameter, model setting, or checkpoint was changed at any point after seeing this benchmark's output, for either system. OpenSLT's fairseq-generate flags match the official Taskfile.yml generate: target verbatim except two documented zero-effect additions (--cpu, --num-workers 0). Uni-Sign's num_beams=4 / max_new_tokens=100 are the documented defaults, unchanged throughout, including after observing the max_new_tokens truncation pattern reported separately below.
max_new_tokens_note: Uni-Sign's predictions show truncation (no terminal punctuation) that rises with clip duration: 3.3% of clips <5s, 10.6% of clips 5-15s, 65.0% of clips 15-31s. This is consistent with the fixed max_new_tokens=100 decoding cap. This was OBSERVED, not corrected: the cap was NOT raised, and the frozen benchmark was NOT altered, truncated, or filtered in response.

openslt.feature_source: CORA/Dataverse DOI 10.34810/DATA693, file ID 51538 (official released I3D test-split features)
compatibility_patches: --cpu (required, no GPU on this machine; zero effect on decoding)
--num-workers 0 (required: macOS spawn-based multiprocessing cannot pickle a fairseq Hydra config Enum; zero effect on decoding)

Cython transpilation of data_utils_fast.pyx/token_block_utils_fast.pyx run by hand before `pip install --editable .` (build-tooling gap in fairseq's setup.py under modern pip, unrelated to macOS/arm64; would fail identically on Linux with a modern toolchain)
pip downgraded to 24.0 inside this env only, to install omegaconf==2.0.6's old-style metadata
openslt.not_tuned: Every fairseq-generate flag matches the official Taskfile.yml generate: target verbatim except the two zero-effect additions above. No decoding parameter was changed after seeing any benchmark output.
openslt.note_on_per_clip_timing: fairseq-generate processes the whole batch in one call; per-clip timing is not independently instrumented (same limitation documented in the pilot_v1 19-clip run). Total batch wall-clock and batch-average are reported instead of per-clip runtimes.

conda env built with CONDA_SUBDIR=osx-arm64 (base conda defaulted to Rosetta/x86_64)
